eval_instructions: Test against real .NET AgentFramework, Node.js, and Python agent projects. The skill MUST use the a365 CLI (a365 develop list-available, a365 develop add-mcp-servers) to manage ToolingManifest.json — never hand-edit it. Verify that McpToolRegistrationService (or equivalent) is wired in agent code. Verify that the permissions handoff is clearly explained to the user. The skill does NOT grant permissions directly — it instructs the user or Global Administrator on what to run.

evals.prompt: Add workiq tools to this agent
evals.description: Full flow on a .NET AgentFramework project — a365 setup not yet run
evals.expected_output: The skill detects .NET AgentFramework, determines agentType and authMode via two-stage question (AI Teammate vs System Agent, then auth mode — with S2S warning if selected), runs a365 develop list-available, asks the user which servers to add, runs a365 develop add-mcp-servers, installs the tooling NuGet package, wires GetMcpToolsAsync in the agent class, registers IMcpToolRegistrationService in Program.cs, explains that a365 setup all will apply permissions, shows how to get a dev token, and validates the build.
expectations: Phase 0B: Agent type question presented — AI Teammate or System Agent
Phase 0B: Auth mode question presented based on agent type selection
Phase 0B: agentType and authMode determined and stored in .a365-workspace-detection.json
Phase 0B: If authMode is S2S, WorkIQ compatibility warning is shown before proceeding to Phase 4
Phase 1: Agent type is detected as .NET AgentFramework
Phase 1: a365 --version is run to verify CLI is installed
Phase 1: a365 develop list-configured is run to check existing servers
Phase 1: AGENTIC_APP_ID is checked in appsettings.json or .env
Phase 2: a365 develop list-available is run and output is shown to the user
Phase 2: User is asked which WorkIQ servers to add
Phase 3: a365 develop add-mcp-servers is run with the selected server name(s)
Phase 3: ToolingManifest.json is NOT hand-edited — CLI command is used exclusively
Phase 3: a365 develop list-configured is run to verify servers appear
Phase 4: dotnet add package Microsoft.Agents.A365.Tooling.Extensions.AgentFramework is run if package is missing
Phase 4: IMcpToolRegistrationService and IMcpToolServerConfigurationService are registered in Program.cs
Phase 4: GetMcpToolsAsync is added to the agent message handler
Phase 4: No tokenOverride parameter is passed to GetMcpToolsAsync
Phase 4: All new code is marked: // A365 WorkIQ — added by add-workiq-tools skill
Phase 5: Blueprint does not exist yet — user is told a365 setup all will apply permissions
Phase 6: a365 develop get-token command is shown to the user
Phase 6: SKIP_TOOLING_ON_ERRORS and BEARER_TOKEN env vars are documented
Phase 6: A WorkIQ dev launch profile is added to launchSettings.json
Phase 7: dotnet build is run and result is shown
Phase 8: Summary includes agent kind, authMode, MCP servers added, permissions status, and dev testing steps

evals.description: Full flow on a Node.js LangChain project — blueprint already exists
evals.expected_output: The skill detects Node.js LangChain, determines agentType and authMode via two-stage question (with S2S warning if selected), runs a365 develop list-available, adds selected servers via CLI, installs @microsoft/agents-a365-tooling, wires A365McpToolClient.getToolsAsync in the agent, adds env vars to .env, explains that a Global Administrator must run a365 setup permissions mcp since blueprint already exists, shows a365 develop get-token, and validates the build.
expectations: Phase 0B: Agent type question presented — AI Teammate or System Agent
Phase 0B: Auth mode question presented based on agent type selection
Phase 0B: agentType and authMode determined and stored in .a365-workspace-detection.json
Phase 0B: If authMode is S2S, WorkIQ compatibility warning is shown before proceeding to Phase 4
Phase 1: Agent type is detected as Node.js LangChain
Phase 1: a365 develop list-configured is run
Phase 1: a365.generated.config.json is found with a non-empty agentBlueprintId
Phase 2: a365 develop list-available is run and output is shown
Phase 2: User is asked which WorkIQ servers to add
Phase 3: a365 develop add-mcp-servers is run
Phase 3: ToolingManifest.json is updated by CLI — not hand-edited
Phase 4: npm install @microsoft/agents-a365-tooling is run if package is missing
Phase 4: A365McpToolClient is imported in the agent entry point
Phase 4: getToolsAsync is called with agentId and userToken
Phase 4: WorkIQ tools are spread into the existing tools array
Phase 4: All new code is marked: // A365 WorkIQ — added by add-workiq-tools skill
Phase 5: Blueprint exists — user is told Global Administrator must run a365 setup permissions mcp
Phase 5: User is told admin must first verify deploymentProjectPath via a365 config display
Phase 5: Updated ToolingManifest.json must be shared with the GA
Phase 6: a365 develop get-token is shown
Phase 6: BEARER_TOKEN and SKIP_TOOLING_ON_ERRORS added to .env
Phase 7: npm install and npm run build succeed
Phase 8: Summary includes agent kind, authMode, MCP servers added, and Global Administrator permissions requirement prominently

evals.prompt: Add Work IQ Mail and Work IQ Calendar to this agent
evals.description: User specifies exact server names — selective install
evals.expected_output: The skill uses the user-provided server names directly, runs a365 develop add-mcp-servers with those two servers, wires agent code, and explains only the permissions relevant to Mail and Calendar.
expectations: Phase 2: User-provided server names ('Work IQ Mail', 'Work IQ Calendar') are used directly without re-prompting
Phase 3: a365 develop add-mcp-servers 'Work IQ Mail' 'Work IQ Calendar' is run as a single command
Phase 3: Both servers appear in a365 develop list-configured output
Phase 4: Agent code is wired to load tools from both servers
Phase 8: Summary lists only the two selected servers

evals.description: Idempotency — WorkIQ servers already in ToolingManifest.json, GetMcpToolsAsync already called
evals.expected_output: The skill detects that the servers are already configured and GetMcpToolsAsync is already wired, skips those steps, and validates the build.
expectations: Phase 0B: .a365-workspace-detection.json is read — agentType and authMode loaded from cache if previously set (no re-questioning)
Phase 1: a365 develop list-configured shows WorkIQ servers already present
Phase 2: User is informed which servers are already configured
Phase 3: a365 develop add-mcp-servers is SKIPPED for already-configured servers
Phase 4: GetMcpToolsAsync / A365McpToolClient presence is detected — wiring is SKIPPED
Phase 7: Build is still run and validated
Phase 8: Summary reports the agent was already partially or fully configured

evals.prompt: Add workiq tools — a365 CLI not installed
evals.expected_output: The skill detects that a365 CLI is not installed, installs it with the dotnet tool install command, verifies the install, then proceeds with the normal flow.
expectations: Phase 1: a365 --version fails — CLI is not installed
Phase 1: dotnet tool install -g Microsoft.Agents.A365.DevTools.Cli --prerelease is run
Phase 1: a365 --version is re-run to confirm install succeeded
Skill does NOT abort — continues with list-available after CLI is installed
Normal flow resumes from Phase 2 onward
